sections.heading: C2 — Driver fitness and impairment
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Driver fitness and impairment

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A01
Prescription and nonprescription medicines can impair driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A01
Check a medicine’s label for driving-related warnings before taking it when you plan to drive. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A01
A medicine warning about operating heavy machinery also means not driving a car or truck. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A01
If unsure about a drug’s driving effects, ask a physician or pharmacist about side effects. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A01
The handbook warns against mixing alcohol with other drugs because the combination can intensify impairment or add harmful side effects. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A01
When illness makes driving unsafe, have someone else drive. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A01
Before each drive, decide whether you are physically and mentally able to drive safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A01
For epilepsy, the handbook calls for a physician’s written attestation that the condition is stable and unlikely to interfere with safe driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A01
Ask the treating doctor whether a heart condition could affect safe driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A01
Stress or strong emotions can reduce concentration and safe-driving ability. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A01
If angry or excited, wait off the road until calm before driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A01
Allow extra trip time when impatience might encourage speeding or risky driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R13 | anchor: A02
An older driver should follow a doctor’s advice to avoid heavy traffic, high-speed traffic or night driving when that advice is given. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec12-R14 | anchor: A02
Medical professionals can use form 32-1800 for a Recommendation for Re-Exam. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec12-R15 | anchor: A02
Form 20-1900 is listed for Driver Medical Evaluation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec12-R16 | anchor: A02
Form 22-1801 is listed for a Report of Eye Examination. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec12-R17 | anchor: A02
Older drivers should drive only when they feel well and able to do so. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec12-R18 | anchor: A02
Older drivers should not drive after taking medication unless their doctor says it is safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec12-R19 | anchor: A02
Stay alert for sudden unsafe moves by other drivers, pedestrians and children. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec12-R20 | anchor: A02
Keep current on traffic laws and safe-driving rules. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec12-R21 | anchor: A02
Older drivers should plan trips and avoid busy, high-speed or personally troubling routes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec12-R22 | anchor: A02
If slow driving holds up traffic, pull off and let it pass, or choose another route or a quieter travel time. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec12-R23 | anchor: A02
Keep the vehicle in safe condition with regular equipment checks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec12-R24 | anchor: A02
Clean the windshield, headlamps and eyeglasses to preserve the driving view, especially at night. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec12-R25 | anchor: A02
Wear a seatbelt on every drive. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec12-R26 | anchor: A03
Needing two or three attempts to parallel park is one of the handbook’s driving-skill self-check concerns. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec12-R27 | anchor: A03
Trouble distinguishing objects at night or prolonged discomfort from headlight glare is a reason to reassess driving vision. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec12-R28 | anchor: A03
For the handbook’s older-driver self-check, trouble keeping pace with traffic or taking a long time to start after a green light is a reason to consider driving ability. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec12-R29 | anchor: A03
Increasing minor vehicle scrapes or dents can be a warning to review driving skills. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec12-R30 | anchor: A03
Missing traffic signs or becoming confused by unfamiliar situations calls for reviewing driving ability. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec12-R31 | anchor: A03
For the handbook’s older-driver self-check, trouble judging distance, seeing nearby or distant objects, or detecting the road edges is a reason to consider driving ability. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec12-R32 | anchor: A03
Health or medication effects, close calls, a serious crash, discomfort at the wheel or fear of getting lost can inform the decision to stop driving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec12-R33 | anchor: A03
A driver who believes safe driving is no longer possible may surrender the license at any driver exam station. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec12-R34 | anchor: A03
Concerns about another driver’s ability may be submitted using Recommendation for Re-Exam form 32-1800. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]
